title: Getting Ready Together
objectives: I can say what listen, share, ready, together, and safe mean.
I can tell how I listen, share, and stay safe at school.
I can use the new words when I talk about our class.
rationale: These five words are the language of the first weeks of school. Listen, share, and together name what children do with other people; ready and safe name how they feel and where they stand when a routine starts. Children act each word out first, then say it in a short sentence. Together and safe are reused all year in talk about teams, helpers, and rules, and share reappears in the feelings unit.

words.def: Pay attention to sounds with your ears.
words.ex: We listen to the story on the rug.
words.ex2: Grandpa and I listen to the rain at night.
words.nonExample: Talking while your teacher talks is not listening.

apps.academic: Listen first, then tell your partner what you heard.
apps.writing: Draw what you heard when you listen.

words.def: Give part of what you have to others.
words.ex: I share my crayons with my table.
words.ex2: At lunch, Dad and I share one big orange.

words.def: Set to start because everything is done.
words.ex: My backpack is on, and I am ready to go.
words.ex2: The table is ready, so we can eat.
words.nonExample: A child still looking for shoes is not ready for the bus.

apps.academic: Show me when you are ready.
apps.writing: Write one thing you do to get ready.

cloze.s: Pencil sharpened, paper out: I am ___ to write.

cloze2.s: Dinner is on the table, so everyone is ___ to eat.

misuse.s: I am ready for school, but I am still in my pajamas and have no shoes.
misuse.why: Ready means set to start, and this child still has things to do.

visual.alt: A backpack with a green check mark beside it.

words.def: With other people, side by side.
words.ex: We build a tall tower together.
words.ex2: My cousins and I sing together in the car.
words.nonExample: Two kids in two different rooms are not together.

apps.writing: Draw yourself and a friend together.

cloze.s: Two friends push the big box ___ so it moves.

cloze2.s: Mom, Dad, and I sit ___ at the dinner table.

misuse.s: I played together with my friend while I sat alone in my room.
misuse.why: Together means with other people, but this child is alone.

visual.alt: Two children fitting puzzle pieces side by side.

words.def: Not in danger and not likely to get hurt.
words.ex: We hold hands to stay safe on the street.
words.ex2: The baby sleeps safe and warm in her bed.
words.nonExample: A hot stove is not safe to touch.

apps.academic: Walking feet keep us safe in the hall.
apps.writing: Write one way to be safe at school.

cloze.s: Wear a helmet to keep your head ___ on a bike.

cloze2.s: The firefighter carried the kitten to a ___ place.

misuse.s: It is safe to run into the street without looking.
misuse.why: Running into a street without looking is dangerous, not safe.

visual.alt: A bright safety vest and a school crossing sign.

passage.title: Room 4 Gets Ready
paras: The bell rang, and Room 4 got ready. Ben sat on the rug and listened to Ms. Ray read.
Then the class shared a big box of blocks. They built a tall tower together.
The tower fell down, but nobody was hurt. Everyone had stayed safe.

qs.why: The class shared a big box of blocks; the story and the rug were not shared out.

qs.q: Why was nobody hurt when the tower fell?
qs.why: The story says everyone had stayed safe, so nobody was hurt.

qs.q: What did the children do together?
qs.why: They built a tall tower together.

study.task: Say each word slowly and clap its parts: lis-ten, share, read-y, to-geth-er, safe. Which word has the most claps?

teacher.overview: Children learn five words for the first weeks of school by acting them out, then hear them in a short read-aloud and say them in short sentences. Everything is oral and gestural; no reading or writing is required.

notes.va.listen.v: Teach with a gesture: cup a hand behind the ear. Listen is an action children choose to do; hear happens on its own. Ask children to listen for a sound in the room and name it.
notes.va.share.v: Model with a real object, such as one big sheet of paper and two children. Some children think share means give away for good; show that it means each person gets a turn or a part.
notes.va.ready.adj: Practice a ready signal, such as hands in lap. Ask what a child must do to be ready, since ready depends on the job: ready for lunch is not ready for the bus.
notes.va.together.adv: Use partner movements, such as walking together and carrying a basket together. Contrast with a child working alone, so the meaning with others is clear.
notes.va.safe.adj: Keep it concrete: walking feet, holding the rail, staying with the group. Avoid scary examples. Ask children for one safe choice, not a list of dangers.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'I want my class to be ready. I sit tall, I put my hands in my lap, and I look at my teacher. Now I am ready to listen. When I listen, I can hear the story. Let's say it together: I am ready to listen.'
discuss: Show me with your body how you look when you are ready.
What can we share at school?
misconceptions: Share means give something away forever.
Listen only means keep your mouth closed.
extend: Make a class chart with pictures: how we listen, how we share, how we stay safe.
Play a quiet game: the teacher whispers a direction and children show they were listening.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit ready and listen in unit 2 when children follow position directions, and share and together in unit 3 when they talk about feelings. Use the words in daily routines all week.

wida.oral: Partner A acts out one word without speaking, such as cupping an ear for listen or handing out a crayon for share. Partner B says the word and a short sentence using it.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (escuchar, compartir, listo, juntos, seguro) have not been reviewed by a native speaker; listo can also mean clever and may need a regional note.
Sense boundary: share is taught only as a verb (give part of what you have); the noun sense is left out.
Sense boundary: listen is paired with, but kept separate from, hear; the unit does not teach hear.
